shortDescription: Add, update, or remove PostgreSQL publication

options.name: ca_cert
options.description: Specifies the name of a file containing SSL certificate authority (CA) certificate(s). If the file exists, the server's certificate will be verified to be signed by one of these authorities.

options.name: cascade
options.description: Drop publication dependencies. Has effect with I(state=absent) only.

options.name: columns
options.description: List of tables and its columns to add to the publication. If no columns are passed for table, it will be published as a whole. Mutually exclusive with I(tables) and I(tables_in_schema).

options.name: comment
options.description: Sets a comment on the publication. To reset the comment, pass an empty string.

options.name: connect_params
options.description: Any additional parameters to be passed to libpg. These parameters take precedence.

options.name: login_db
options.description: Name of the database to connect to and where the publication state will be changed. The V(db) alias is deprecated and will be removed in version 5.0.0.

options.name: login_host
options.description: Host running the database. If you have connection issues when using C(localhost), try to use C(127.0.0.1) instead.

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password this module should use to establish its PostgreSQL session.

options.name: login_port
options.description: Database port to connect to. The C(port) alias is deprecated and will be removed in the next major release. Use C(login_port) instead.

options.name: login_unix_socket
options.description: Path to a Unix domain socket for local connections.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The username this module should use to establish its PostgreSQL session.

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the publication to add, update, or remove.

options.name: owner
options.description: Publication owner. If I(owner) is not defined, the owner will be set as I(login_user) or I(session_role).

options.name: parameters
options.description: Dictionary with optional publication parameters. Available parameters depend on PostgreSQL version.

options.name: rowfilters
options.description: Optional dictionary of row filters to apply to I(tables) or I(columns) of the publication. Mutually exclusive with I(tables_in_schema).

options.name: session_role
options.description: Switch to session_role after connecting. The specified session_role must be a role that the current login_user is a member of. Permissions checking for SQL commands is carried out as though the session_role were the one that had logged in originally.

options.name: ssl_cert
options.description: Specifies the file name of the client SSL certificate.

options.name: ssl_key
options.description: Specifies the location for the secret key used for the client certificate.

options.name: ssl_mode
options.description: Determines whether or with what priority a secure SSL TCP/IP connection will be negotiated with the server. See U(https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/static/libpq-ssl.html) for more information on the modes. Default of C(prefer) matches libpq default.

options.name: state
options.description: The publication state.

options.name: tables
options.description: List of tables to add to the publication. If no value is set all tables are targeted. If the publication already exists for specific tables and I(tables) is not passed, nothing will be changed. If you need to add all tables to the publication with the same name, drop existent and create new without passing I(tables). Mutually exclusive with I(tables_in_schema) and I(columns).

options.name: tables_in_schema
options.description: Specifies a list of schemas to add to the publication to replicate changes for all tables in those schemas. If you want to remove all schemas, explicitly pass an empty list C([]). Supported since PostgreSQL 15. Mutually exclusive with I(tables) and I(columns).

options.name: trust_input
options.description: If C(false), check whether values of parameters I(name), I(tables), I(owner), I(session_role), I(params) are potentially dangerous. It makes sense to use C(false) only when SQL injections via the parameters are possible.
